key_insight: Nonlinearity-subtracted DMD (NSDMD) uses nonlinear forcing information from Navier–Stokes snapshots to learn a low-rank linear operator that approximates mean-flow linearized turbulent dynamics.
engineering_relevance: This makes resolvent-style linear analysis feasible as a post-processing tool for DNS/LES from general CFD codes, including complex geometries and aircraft-scale flows.
method: Compute DMD on perturbation dynamics while explicitly subtracting the contribution of nonlinear terms.
Use snapshots of the nonlinear forcing to isolate the effective linear operator.
Apply the learned operator for data-driven resolvent analysis on turbulent flow datasets.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports demonstrations on both a minimal channel flow and a full aircraft model using DNS and LES datasets.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on the quality and availability of snapshots for the nonlinear terms, which may be challenging in noisy or incomplete simulation data.
paper_title: Data-driven linear analysis of turbulent flows
